title: Journal Examples: 16 Real Entries to Copy (Every Type)
description: 16 journal examples you can copy: daily, gratitude, reflective, dream, goal, venting, travel, prayer and bullet entries, with tips to write your own.
h1: Journal examples: 16 entries for every kind of journal
intro: A journal entry can be three lines about your day, a list of things you are grateful for, a dream you remember, or a letter you will never send. Below are 16 short journal examples, one for each common type, with a note on how to write your own. Pick one style and try it today.

writer.title: My entry
writer.hint: Pick an example below and write your own version.

sections.h2: How to write a journal entry (the basic shape)

blocks.p: This page is about personal journals, the kind you keep for yourself. If you were looking for academic journals, those are published magazines of research, which is a different meaning of the word.
Almost every good journal entry has three parts. You do not have to follow them, but they help when you are stuck.

ol: **The date** at the top, so you can read back later.
**What happened or what is on your mind.** One event, feeling or idea.
**Your thoughts about it.** Why it matters, what you learned, or what comes next.

blocks.p: That is it. The examples below change the middle part to fit different journal types. For more help, see [what to write in a journal](/what-to-write-in-a-journal/).

example.label: Daily journal
example.text:
Woke up late and missed the 7:40 bus.
Got to work flustered but the morning was quiet.
Lunch with Priya. She is moving to Denver in August.
I am happy for her and sad for me.
Evening: leftovers, one episode, bed by 11.

blocks.p: **How to write it:** tell your day in order, then add one line about how you feel. A daily diary is exactly this.

example.label: One line a day
example.text:
Tue: Rain. Finished the book. Cried at the end.
Wed: Tried the new taco place. Too spicy, still good.
Thu: Long day. Called Dad. He sounded tired.
Fri: Payday. Bought flowers for no reason.
Sat: Slept until 10. Bliss.

blocks.p: **How to write it:** one sentence, every day, no more. Great for busy people. See our [one line a day journal](/one-line-a-day-journal/).

example.label: Mood journal
example.title: Mood: 6 out of 10
example.text:
Morning: 4. Grumpy, slept badly.
Afternoon: 7. Good meeting, felt useful.
Evening: 6. Tired but calm.
Pattern? Bad sleep, bad mornings. Again.

blocks.p: **How to write it:** rate your mood, then write why. Over weeks, a mood journal shows patterns.

example.label: Gratitude journal
example.title: Today I am grateful for
example.text:
1. The man who held the door when my hands were full.
2. Cold watermelon after the walk home.
3. My sister's voice note, even though it was 6 minutes long.
Small things. They added up to a good day.

blocks.p: **How to write it:** three specific good things. Specific is the key. More in our [gratitude journal](/gratitude-journal/) guide.

example.label: Reflective journal
example.title: The presentation
example.text:
What happened: I presented the budget to the team.
How I felt: shaky at first, then fine.
What went well: my slides were clear.
What I would change: practice out loud, not just in my head.
Next time: rehearse twice the night before.

blocks.p: **How to write it:** describe an event, then think about what went well and what you would do differently. See our full guide to the [reflective journal](/reflective-journal/).

sections.h2: Dream, goal and venting journal examples

example.label: Dream journal
example.title: The house with too many doors
example.text:
I was in my grandma's house but it had extra hallways.
Every door opened onto a beach.
I was looking for my keys and felt rushed.
Woke up at 6:12. Feeling: confused, a little anxious.
Maybe about the move?

blocks.p: **How to write it:** write as soon as you wake up, before the details fade. Add how you felt. Keep the journal by your bed.

example.label: Goal journal
example.title: Goal: save $1,000 by December
example.text:
Saved so far: $240.
This week: cooked at home 5 nights. Saved about $40.
Hard part: coffee runs. $18 this week.
Next week: bring coffee from home 3 days.
I am closer than I thought.

blocks.p: **How to write it:** state the goal, track progress, name the obstacle, set one next step.

example.label: Venting
example.text:
I am SO annoyed. Third time this month he cancelled last minute.
I cleaned, I cooked, I waited.
I feel like I am the only one who tries.
Okay. Breathing. I think I need to tell him how this feels.
Not tonight though. Tomorrow, calmly.

blocks.p: **How to write it:** let it all out, then end with one calmer line. Venting on paper is often safer than venting by text.

sections.h2: Travel, prayer and letter journal examples

example.label: Travel journal
example.text:
Climbed so many hills my legs are shaking.
Best thing: custard tarts still warm from the oven.
Got lost in Alfama and found a tiny bar with live music.
The singer looked right at us during the sad song.
Tomorrow: the tram, the castle, and more tarts.

blocks.p: **How to write it:** focus on senses and small details. Those are what you forget first. Try this on your next trip.

example.label: Prayer journal
example.title: Dear Lord,
example.text:
Thank You for a safe drive and for Mom's good test results.
I pray for Jen as she starts her new job.
Please help me be patient with the kids this week.
I give You my worry about money.
Amen.

blocks.p: **How to write it:** thanks, prayers for others, your own needs. See our [prayer journal examples](/prayer-journal-examples/) for more.

example.label: Unsent letter
example.title: Dear Grandpa,
example.text:
It has been two years and I still reach for my phone to call you.
I made your chili on Sunday. It was not as good.
I got the job you said I would get.
I wish you could see it. I miss you every day.

blocks.p: **How to write it:** write to someone directly. It is just for you and never sent.

example.label: Free writing
example.text:
Okay I do not know what to write. The coffee is too hot.
I keep thinking about whether to take the class.
I think I want to but I am scared of being the oldest one.
That is a silly reason. I am going to sign up today.

blocks.p: **How to write it:** write without stopping for five to ten minutes, first thing in the morning. Do not edit. See [morning journal prompts](/morning-journal-prompts/).

sections.h2: More journal examples: bullet, project, self discovery and habit

example.label: Bullet journal
example.text:
x Pay phone bill
x Gym, legs
> Call insurance (moved to Monday)
o Lunch with Kim at 1
- Felt good after the gym. Kim is pregnant!

blocks.p: **How to write it:** short bullets with simple symbols. x for done, > for moved, o for events, a dash for notes. See [bullet journal ideas](/bullet-journal-ideas/).

example.label: Project journal
example.text:
Planted tomatoes and basil in the raised bed.
The left corner gets less sun. Seedlings there are smaller.
Lesson: move the peppers to the right side next year.
Next: water every morning, check for slugs.

blocks.p: **How to write it:** keep one journal for a hobby or project. Note what you did, what you learned, and what you will try next.

example.label: Self discovery
example.title: When do I feel most like myself?
example.text:
Cooking for friends with music on.
Long walks with no destination.
Not at big parties, even though I keep saying yes.
Maybe I should say yes to smaller plans instead.

blocks.p: **How to write it:** pick one deep question and answer honestly. Find more in [journal prompts for self discovery](/journal-prompts-for-self-discovery/).

example.label: Habit journal
example.text:
Water: 6 out of 7 days
Reading: 4 out of 7 days
Phone off by 10: 2 out of 7 days. Oops.
The phone one is hardest. I will charge it in the kitchen.

blocks.p: **How to write it:** track one to three habits, then add a short note about what helped or got in the way.

sections.h2: Tips to write your own journal entries

head: If you want to
Start with example
rows: 1. Daily journal or 2. One line a day
Calm down after a bad day

ul: **Copy a shape, not the words.** Use the structure of an example above and fill it with your own life.
**Keep lines short.** You are not writing an essay. Short lines read well later.
**Add one feeling.** Even a daily log becomes a journal when you add how you felt.
**Use real details.** Names, times, food, weather. They bring memories back.
**Mix types.** A daily entry can end with one gratitude line or one prayer.

blocks.tip: For more ready-to-copy pages, see [diary entry examples](/diary-entry-examples/) and [journal examples for students](/journal-examples-for-students/).

faq.q: What is an example of a journal entry?
faq.a: A simple example: "Monday. Missed the bus and got to work late. Felt stressed but the day was quiet. Lunch with a friend who is moving away. Happy for her, sad for me." It has a date, what happened, and how the writer felt. That is all a journal entry needs.

faq.q: How do you write a good journal entry?
faq.a: Start with the date. Write about one event, feeling or idea in specific detail. Add how you felt and what you think about it. End with a thought, lesson or next step. Be honest and write like you talk. Short and real beats long and polished.

faq.q: What are the different types of journals?
faq.a: Common types include daily journals, gratitude journals, reflective journals, dream journals, mood journals, goal journals, travel journals, prayer journals, bullet journals and one line a day journals. Many people mix two or three types in one notebook.

faq.q: How long should a journal entry be?
faq.a: Anywhere from one sentence to a few pages. Most of the examples above are 40 to 70 words, which takes a few minutes to write. Write enough to capture the moment and your feeling about it, and stop when you are done.

faq.q: Can I write a journal entry about everyday life?
faq.a: Yes, and you should. Everyday entries are often the ones people treasure most later, because ordinary days are the easiest to forget. Write what you ate, who you saw, and one thing you noticed. That is a complete entry.
